by: Claude Code (opus), titles and abstracts only

question.outcome: Kidney stones, or oxalate in urine

decisions.reason: Adults, vitamin C supplements and kidney stones match, but the pooled studies look observational (dose-based odds ratios; RCTs called for), not randomised trials.

question.population: Adults with iron-deficiency anaemia taking iron tablets
question.intervention: Vitamin C tablets added to iron tablets

decisions.reason: Tests vitamin C-rich fruits or juices eaten with meals in females and children, not vitamin C tablets added to iron tablets in anaemic adults.
Pools RCTs of vitamin C on haemoglobin and ferritin, but in hemodialysis patients on standard anaemia care, not adults taking iron tablets alone.

question.population: Children and adults in the general community
question.outcome: How many people catch colds (or respiratory infections)

Pooled vitamin C trials separately for ARI occurrence, but included adults only, not children.

question.outcome: How many people catch colds (results for this group apart)

Dialysis patients and lipid peroxidation markers; a different population and outcome.

Pooled placebo-controlled trials of prophylactic vitamin C on cold incidence with a subgroup of marathon runners, skiers and soldiers.
Pooled placebo-controlled trials of prophylactic vitamin C on cold incidence with a subgroup of marathon runners, skiers and soldiers.

question.intervention: Vitamin C every day, or started when a cold begins
question.outcome: How long colds last and how bad they are

decisions.reason: Vitamin C vs placebo with pooled duration and severity matches, but the outcome is respiratory tract infections in general rather than colds specifically.
Pools vitamin C trials on how long infections last, but only in adults and for acute respiratory infections in general rather than colds.

Pools placebo-controlled trials of daily and cold-onset vitamin C in adults and children for cold duration and severity.

Pools placebo-controlled trials of daily and cold-onset vitamin C in adults and children for cold duration and severity.
Pools placebo-controlled trials of daily and cold-onset vitamin C in adults and children for cold duration and severity.
Title matches the question on every part, but there is no abstract, so the methods and pooling could not be checked.

question.intervention: Vitamin C supplements (alone, or with results for vitamin C apart)
